title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is navigating a landscape marked by geopolitical tensions and regulatory hurdles, with European players voicing concerns over competitiveness. Meanwhile, funding and partnerships continue to shape the trajectory of defense and commercial space initiatives.

themes.title: EU Space Act Concerns
themes.body: The European space industry is raising alarms that the proposed EU Space Act could hinder its competitiveness against global players. This regulatory scrutiny comes at a time when agility is crucial for maintaining relevance in a fast-evolving sector.

themes.title: Geopolitics and Space Opportunities
themes.body: As geopolitical dynamics shift, companies like SpinLaunch are positioning themselves to capitalize on new opportunities. The evolving landscape suggests that innovation may be the best defense against external pressures.

themes.title: Funding for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent FY27 budget markup, which adds $1.4 billion to space resilience, reflects a growing recognition of the need for robust defense capabilities in orbit. This influx of capital could spur advancements in technologies that ensure operational continuity.

themes.title: Tactical Constellation Collaborations
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, signaling a trend toward collaborative approaches in defense space initiatives. Such partnerships may be essential for navigating the complexities of modern military requirements.
